label: Annual energy production (AEP)
definition: The energy produced by a system over one year.
comment: It is usually given in kWh/year, MWh/year or GWh/year and is the main output of energy yield assessments.

label: Availability factor
definition: The fraction of time during which a system is able to operate.
comment: For turbines it can also be the probability that the wind speed lies between cut-in and cut-out speeds.

label: Avoided emissions
definition: The greenhouse-gas emissions avoided by producing energy from a renewable source instead of a reference source.
comment: They are usually given in tonnes of CO2 per year.

label: Capacity factor
definition: The ratio of the energy actually produced by a system over a period to the energy it would produce at rated power over the same period.
comment: It is usually given in percent; typical values are 20-45 % for wind turbines, 15-25 % for PV and 30-60 % for hydropower plants.

label: Efficiency
definition: The ratio of useful output energy or power to input energy or power of a system or component.
comment: In the corpus it is mostly the efficiency of turbines, PV modules or conversion chains, given in percent.

label: Energy potential
definition: The amount of power or energy that a resource could provide at a site or in a region under stated assumptions.
comment: Studies distinguish theoretical, technical and economic potentials; the assumption is given by the value and its study.

label: Energy production
definition: The energy produced by a system over a stated period.
comment: Unlike the annual energy production, the period can be a season, a month or the whole study period.

label: Firm energy
definition: The energy that a plant can supply with a stated reliability over a period.
comment: It is used for hydropower planning.

label: Firm power
definition: The power that a plant can supply with a stated reliability, for example 90 % of the time.
comment: It is used for run-of-river hydropower, where it is derived from the flow-duration curve.

label: Installed capacity
definition: The rated power of a plant or a set of plants.
comment: It is given in kW, MW or GW.

label: Mean power output
definition: The average electrical power delivered by a turbine, plant or system over a period.
comment: It is given in kW or MW and equals the energy produced divided by the duration of the period.

label: Most probable wind speed
definition: The wind speed with the highest probability density in the wind-speed distribution.
comment: For a Weibull distribution it is c((k-1)/k)^(1/k).

label: Pumped water volume
definition: The volume of water pumped by a system over a period.
comment: It is used for wind or solar water-pumping systems.

label: Turbulence intensity
definition: The ratio of the standard deviation of the wind speed to the mean wind speed over a short period.
comment: It is usually computed over 10-minute periods and affects turbine loads and power curves.

label: Wake loss
definition: The reduction of energy production of a wind farm caused by the wakes of upstream turbines.
comment: It is given in percent of the gross production.

label: Wind power density
definition: The mean kinetic power of the wind per unit area swept perpendicular to the flow.
comment: It is computed as ½ρv³ averaged over the wind-speed distribution and given in W/m²; it is the basis of wind power classes.

label: Wind speed carrying maximum energy
definition: The wind speed that contributes the largest share of the wind energy.
comment: For a Weibull distribution it is c((k+2)/k)^(1/k); it guides the choice of the rated speed of turbines.
